column2: req_desc

Account sign-up and sign-in
Visitors create an account with email, password and display name, sign in and out with a session cookie, and get the exact validation and credential errors listed in API.

Blank stage starter
A new account lands in an empty workspace, and creating a set from the 'Blank stage' starter shows the starting layer tree listed in Seed data.

Public demo stage
The public '/' shows the booth dialog over the shell running the 'Low Tide Tunnel' demo, which plays from the beat transport without an account.

Gapless op log
Every committed edit to a set is one op that gets the next gapless sequence number and its target's version bump, committed together, and the ops can be read back in order.

Build the stage with gizmos
The VJ adds primitives and moves, rotates and scales them with gizmos under grid and angle snapping, and every committed change survives a reload.

Layer parenting
Layers can be reparented in the layer tree by drag or keyboard, and a move that would make a layer its own ancestor is refused with 422.

Cameras and the active camera
Camera layers carry field of view and near and far planes within the ranges in Business rules, and the stage draws through the set's active camera.

Keyboard layer tree
Arrow keys walk, expand and collapse the layer tree, and the focused row is the selected layer, so no pointer is needed.

Provider-confirmed asset upload
An uploaded GLB or texture becomes 'ready' only after object storage confirms its bytes, and a failed store leaves it 'upload failed' and unusable.

Bind models and textures
The VJ uploads a GLB and a texture, binds them to a model layer and a material texture slot, and sees the model drawn and the texture name in the slot.

Dependents count
Each asset's dependents count equals the number of live layers, materials and scripts that reference it, recomputed after every committed edit.

Guarded asset delete
Deleting an asset that has dependents or appears in a published show version is refused with 409 listing the dependents or the show versions, and any other asset, including one whose upload failed, is removed from the shelf and from object storage.

Assets stored as uploaded
Asset bytes in object storage and from the content endpoint are byte-identical to the uploaded file and match the sha256 the API reports.

Shader compile feedback
Saving a GLSL layer compiles it in the browser, marks error lines in the editor gutter and announces 'Compiled' or the first error line, while the stage keeps the last good program.

Shader version history
Every shader save creates the next numbered version with its sha256, author and time, listed newest first in the shader history.

Byte-exact shader restore
Restoring shader version N creates a new latest version whose source is byte-identical to N and leaves earlier history unchanged.

Shader editing journey
The VJ writes a broken shader, reads the line-numbered error, fixes it, saves several versions and restores an older one onto the stage.

Live node graph
A Beat clock to LFO to Remap to Layer property chain drives that property on every drawn frame while the transport plays.

Keyboard wire picker
A node-graph wire can be connected entirely from the keyboard through the 'Connect wire' dialog's port lists.

Graph wiring rules
The server refuses wires that start from an input or end at an output, fill an occupied input or close a cycle, with the 422 codes in Business rules.

Beat-locked keys
Keys are stored in ticks of 96 per beat, snap to the nearest quarter beat at the playhead, and show bars:beats with seconds at the set BPM.

BPM change keeps bars and beats
Changing the set's BPM keeps every key on the same bar:beat and recomputes only the seconds shown.

Scrub to the beat
The VJ selects a layer, drags a scrub field while the stage redraws each frame, commits on release, and keys the value onto the beat timeline.

Scrub field input
Scrub fields change by 0.1 per pixel dragged or per arrow press, and by 0.01 with Shift, except the BPM field as qualified in Interactions; Enter commits and Escape reverts.

Sandboxed beat scripts
A script's onBeat(ctx) runs once per beat while the transport plays, isolated from the page and the network, and can set layer properties on the stage.

Script errors keep the stage running
A script that throws or runs too long is stopped and reported in the Console tab and a live region while the stage keeps drawing.

Custom plugin nodes
A script that registers a node makes it appear in the node graph's Add node list, and wiring it drives a layer just like a built-in node.

Capability invite links
The owner creates a single-use editor or viewer invite link, and the signed-in guest who accepts it joins the set with that role.

Role permissions
Editors may edit, viewers reach no write endpoint (403), and only the owner invites, publishes, rolls back, deletes assets and force-releases locks.

Presence and selection
Every editor open in a set sees each other editor's name, cursor colour and selected layer, updated within two seconds.

Server-clock lock leases
Layer locks are granted, renewed and expired by the server clock with a 30-second lease, and the lock icon follows only server lock events, whatever the device clock says.

Co-editing under locks
The guest VJ takes a layer lock and edits that layer while the owner sees the lock icon and the committed values, then releases the lock.

One lock winner
When several lock requests for one layer arrive at once, exactly one is granted and every other gets 409 naming the holder.

Stale writes refused
A write whose base version is older than its target's current version is refused with 409 and never merged.

Conflict dialog
A refused stale edit opens the 'Someone changed this layer first' dialog, where Keep theirs discards the edit and Reapply mine commits it on the current version.

Exactly-once ops
A replayed client op id returns the original response without applying the op again, and reusing an id for a different op is refused.

Offline queue banner
While offline, edits queue in the browser and the banner shows the live count of changes waiting to sync.

Reconnect and replay
When the connection returns, the browser replays its queue in order and catches up on missed ops, and every queued op is applied exactly once.

Immutable show versions
Publishing freezes the working set into a bundle in object storage and makes it live only after storage confirms it, and the bundle's bytes and sha256 never change.

Venue show link
The show link plays the live version without sign-in, shows its version number and sha256, serves the exact stored bundle, and exposes no members, emails or unpublished versions.

One-action rollback
Rolling back atomically re-points the show link to the previous published version, which serves the same bytes it served when first published.

Publish and roll back at the venue
The owner publishes, the venue tech's open show link switches to the new version, a broken publish is rolled back, and the show link returns to the good version.

Byte-identical export
Exporting a set stores a zip in object storage whose download is byte-identical to the stored object and matches the reported sha256.

Import as a new set
Importing an exported zip stores the upload byte for byte and creates a new set with the same layer tree, keys, graph, scripts, shaders and assets.

Export and import journey
The VJ exports a set, downloads the zip, imports it, and opens the new set with the same scene.

Asset storage outage
With object storage unreachable, uploads, publishing and export return 503 with the storage banner, the live show keeps its version, and editing continues.

Live collaboration outage
With Valkey unreachable, lock requests return 503 with the collaboration banner, edits still commit to the op log, and other editors catch up within five seconds.

Activity log
Every committed op, publish, rollback, activation, asset upload or delete, member join, lock force-release, export and import appears in the set's activity log with who, what and when.

Degraded night journey
The VJ works through a storage outage and a collaboration outage, sees honest banners and refusals, and reviews the activity log afterwards.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on port 4173 (or APP_PUBLIC_PORT) and answers the health check.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start and is never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Server boundary
The server is same-origin, enforces the body size limits, never serves source files or credentials, and follows the stated order of errors.

Responsive shell
At 1024 pixels wide and above, the fixed shell fills the window with no document scroll; below that it collapses to a drawer and a bottom icon row, with no horizontal overflow at any width.

Keyboard dialogs and shortcuts
Every dialog keeps Tab inside itself, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener, and the published shortcuts work whichever control in their region has focus.

Autosave announcements
Edits commit on release, on blur or after two seconds idle, and the Autosave live region announces the save state with the exact copy.

Booth-dark look
Every screen uses the booth-dark palette, the Arimo and PT Sans typefaces, dense rows and the blue value numerals described in Visual design.

Shell composition
The workbench dock, set menubar, stage viewport, rig panel and beat timeline dock are arranged as Visual design describes, with the booth dialog on the public page.

Motion and reduced motion
Hover fills, drawer collapse and the stage loop follow the timings in Motion and effects, nothing moves while idle, and reduced motion gives the instant substitute.

Real stage rendering
Real WebGL draws the stage, shaders, node-graph output and timeline playback from the committed set state, not images or faked values.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the app.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, each with its name, version and licence.
Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or Zlib, and the fonts are under OFL-1.1.
The app stores state only in PostgreSQL, MinIO and Valkey. It uses no other database, no SQLite and no state files on disk.
The running app makes no request to any third-party origin. Fonts, icons and scripts are served from the app itself.
The provided service configuration and its seeded credentials are left unchanged.
The npm lockfile is committed, and install uses it without modifying it.
